title: Sid Catlett's death on Easter Sunday
summary: Catlett returned to Chicago and dropped dead backstage at the Opera House on Easter Sunday; Saunders helped identify his body.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, Sid eventually moved back here.
Well, just before his death, he come back to Chicago here and was working at the -- you remember, he was working at the Jazz, Ltd.
With -- and then, because they would bring in one person. One time they had Sidney Bechet.
Right, Miff Mole, and then they brought Sid Catlett in, and so he was living here. And, like I say, we were very, very close. And he dropped dead in 1951 or '52, I can't --
Wasn't it backstage at the Opera House?
Backstage at the Opera House, on a Easter Sunday.

And he had given my wife and I a Easter egg, saying -- he always called me brother. And he had sent this Easter egg to us for Easter Sunday. That was on Easter Sunday and he went to the concert and he dropped dead. I went to help identify his body with his father at the morgue, to get his things and all that.
Duke Grohner said that Sid was standing with Duke and his wife. And he just --
